entry.title: CDS Performance Analysis Understanding Dependencies and Complexity Metrics
entry.content:
Introduction

ABAP CDS provides a powerful way to push data-intensive processing to the database layer. However, simply moving logic into CDS does not guarantee that every query will perform well. 

In real projects,  CDS views containing multiple layers, joins, associations, calculated fields, and aggregations. The top-level CDS may look simple, while the generated SQL can be considerably more complex. 

In this blog, let's take a practical example of a Sales Order Analytics CDS and understand how we can analyze its dependency structure using the Dependency Analyzer in ADT.

1. Business Requirement 

Let's assume the business wants a report containing: 

  • Sales Order  
  • Sales Order Item  
  • Sales Organization  
  • Customer  
  • Material  
  • PlantThe application should allow users to filter sales order by:
    • Sales Organization  
    • Created On  
    • Customer A simple implementation might look like this:

       

      At first sight, this looks straightforward. 

    • But let's see what happens when the CDS stack becomes more complicated 2. Create the Basic CDS View 
    • First, let's create a basic CDS view for Sales Order Item.  
@AbapCatalog.viewEnhancementCategory: [#NONE]
@AccessControl.authorizationCheck: #NOT_REQUIRED
@EndUserText.label: 'For Item table of sales order'
@Metadata.ignorePropagatedAnnotations: true
define view entity ZI_SO_ITEM as select from vbap
{
     key vbeln as SalesOrder,
  key posnr as SalesOrderItem,

      matnr as Material,
      werks as Plant,
      vrkme as SalesUnit,
      waerk as Currency
}

This CDS is directly reading from the VBAP database table. 

The dependency at this stage is very simple: 

3. Create Sales Order Header CDS

Now we need header information from VBAK.

@AbapCatalog.viewEnhancementCategory: [#NONE]
@AccessControl.authorizationCheck: #NOT_REQUIRED
@EndUserText.label: 'For Sales order Header'
@Metadata.ignorePropagatedAnnotations: true
define view entity ZI_SOM_HEADER as select from vbak
{
    key vbeln as SalesOrder,

      auart as SalesDocumentType,
      vkorg as SalesOrganization,
      vtweg as DistributionChannel,
      spart as Division,
      kunnr as Customer,
      erdat as CreatedOn
}

  

4. Create the Composite CDS 

Now we combine the Sales Order Header and Item information.

@EndUserText.label: 'Sales Order Analytics Interface' 
@AccessControl.authorizationCheck: #NOT_REQUIRED   
define view entity ZI_SO_ANALYTICS 
  as select from ZI_SO_ITEM as Item 
    inner join ZI_SO_HEADER as Header 
      on Header.SalesOrder = Item.SalesOrder 
{ 
  key Item.SalesOrder, 
  key Item.SalesOrderItem, 
      Header.SalesDocumentType, 
      Header.SalesOrganization, 
      Header.DistributionChannel, 
      Header.Division, 
      Header.Customer, 
      Header.CreatedOn, 
      Item.Material, 
      Item.Plant, 
      Item.OrderQuantity, 
      Item.SalesUnit, 
      Item.NetValue, 
      Item.Currency 

}

Now our dependency structure becomes: 

This is a simple CDS stack. 

But let's make the example more realistic.

5. Add Customer Information

Suppose the business wants the customer name. 

We can create another CDS.

@AbapCatalog.viewEnhancementCategory: [#NONE]
@AccessControl.authorizationCheck: #NOT_REQUIRED
@EndUserText.label: 'For Customer'
@Metadata.ignorePropagatedAnnotations: true
define view entity ZI_CUSTOMER1 as select from kna1
{
     key kunnr as Customer,
      name1 as CustomerName,
      land1 as Country
}

Now modify the composite CDS. 

@AbapCatalog.viewEnhancementCategory: [#NONE]
@AccessControl.authorizationCheck: #NOT_REQUIRED
@EndUserText.label: 'For Analytics'
@Metadata.ignorePropagatedAnnotations: true
define view entity ZI_SO_ANALYTICS as select from ZI_SO_ITEM as Item
inner join ZI_SOM_HEADER as Header on Header.SalesOrder = Item.SalesOrder
left outer join ZI_CUSTOMER1 as customer on customer.Customer = Header.Customer
left outer join zi_material as Material on Material.Matnr = Item.Material
{
    key Item.SalesOrder,
  key Item.SalesOrderItem,
      Header.SalesDocumentType,
      Header.SalesOrganization,
      Header.DistributionChannel,
      Header.Division,
      Header.Customer,
      Header.CreatedOn,
      customer.Country,
      Item.Material,
      Item.Plant,
//Item.OrderQuantity,
      Item.SalesUnit,
      Material.Matnr,
      Material.Mbrsh,
//Item.NetValue,
      Item.Currency
}

 Our dependency tree now looks like: 

6.  Create a consumption view 

Now you want to add the consumption view. 

Create

@AbapCatalog.viewEnhancementCategory: [#NONE]
@AccessControl.authorizationCheck: #NOT_REQUIRED
@EndUserText.label: 'For Analytics'
@Metadata.ignorePropagatedAnnotations: true
define view entity ZC_SO_ANALYTICS as select from ZI_SO_ANALYTICS
{
    key SalesOrder,
    key SalesOrderItem,
    SalesDocumentType,
    SalesOrganization,
    DistributionChannel,
    Division,
    Customer,
    CreatedOn,
    Country,
    Material,
    Plant,
    SalesUnit,
    Matnr,
    Mbrsh,
    Currency
}

 

7.Analyze the CDS Using Dependency Analyzer

Open ZC_SO_ANALYTICS 

in ADT. 

Then: 

Right Click → Open With → Dependency Analyzer 

You can click on Dependency Analyzer

This is a tree What all table,joins,associations you have used in the consumption views

This is the actual graph where we can see all the involvement table in consumption view

It will show you what all the table that you have been used in your views

Conclusion

CDS provides a powerful approach for implementing Code Pushdown and performing data-intensive operations at the database level. However, simply using CDS does not automatically guarantee optimal performance.

As we have seen with the Sales Order Analytics example, a seemingly simple consumption CDS can depend on multiple CDS layers, database tables, joins, associations, calculations, and aggregations. Therefore, understanding the complete CDS stack is an important first step in performance analysis.

The Dependency Analyzer in ADT provides valuable insight into this structure through:

SQL Dependency Tree – helps understand the hierarchy and data sources involved.
SQL Dependency Graph – provides a visual representation of dependencies and helps identify unnecessary branches.
Complexity Metrics – provides an overview of tables, joins, unions, functions, CAST operations, and CASE expressions used by the CDS.

However, these metrics should be treated as indicators rather than direct proof of a performance problem. A CDS with many joins may still perform well, while a seemingly simple CDS can have an expensive execution plan.

Therefore, an effective CDS performance analysis should follow this approach:

The key takeaway is:

Don't optimize CDS based only on how complex the source code looks. Understand what SQL is generated, how the database executes it, identify the actual bottleneck, and then optimize based on measurable results.

This dependency analysis gives us a strong foundation for the next step of CDS performance tuning—analyzing the generated SQL and execution plan to identify the operations that are actually consuming database resources.

entry.title: SAP RAP Hierarchical BO: Complete Guide to Modeling, Behavior, and Fiori UI
entry.content:
Introduction: 

The ABAP RESTful Application Programming Model (RAP) provides a modern and standardized approach for developing transactional business applications. It enables developers to build business objects that can be consumed through OData services and integrated seamlessly with SAP Fiori elements. 

In this blog, we will explore an end-to-end implementation of a managed RAP Business Object for Agency and Employee Management, where an Agency can have multiple Employees and employees can be organized into a hierarchical structure based on their manager relationships.

The implementation demonstrates how the Agency and Employee entities are modeled as a parent-child business object, with draft-enabled processing, transactional behavior, lifecycle handling, and hierarchical employee management. 

The Employee entity additionally supports manager-employee relationships and hierarchy-based processing, including sibling ordering and cascading operations. Business rules are implemented at the RAP behavior level to ensure that the data entering the business object satisfies the required business conditions.

Requirement:

Consider an organization that manages multiple agencies. 

Each agency has: 

  • Agency ID 
  • Agency Name 
  • Address 
  • Country 
  • Phone 
  • Email 
  • Web Address 

Each agency can have multiple employees. 

Each employee has: 

  • Employee ID 
  • First Name 
  • Last Name 
  • Salary 
  • Salary Currency 
  • Manager 
  • Sibling Order Number 

The important requirement is that employees should be organized hierarchically.

For example:

Agency A001 
│ 
├── Employee 100 
│   │ 
│   ├── Employee 101 
│   │ 
│   └── Employee 102 
│ 
└── Employee 200 

Here: 

Employee 100 
   | 
   +-- Employee 101 
   +-- Employee 102 

Employee 100 is the manager of Employees 101 and 102.

Therefore, the database needs to store the manager relationship.

Agency Database Table:

@EndUserText.label : 'Agency Table'

@AbapCatalog.tableCategory : #TRANSPARENT
@AbapCatalog.deliveryClass : #A
@AbapCatalog.dataMaintenance : #RESTRICTED

key client            : abap.clnt not null;
key agency            : /dmo/agency_id not null;
name                  : /dmo/agency_name;
street                : /dmo/street;
postal_code           : /dmo/postal_code;
city                  : /dmo/city;
country_code          : land1;
phone_number          : /dmo/phone_number;
email_address         : /dmo/email_address;
web_address           : /dmo/web_address;
local_created_by      : abp_creation_user;
local_created_at      : abp_creation_tstmpl;
local_last_changed_by : abp_locinst_lastchange_user;

}

 Employee Database Table:

@EndUserText.label : 'Employee table'
@AbapCatalog.enhancement.category : #NOT_EXTENSIBLE

@AbapCatalog.dataMaintenance : #RESTRICTED

@Semantics.amount.currencyCode : 'zbrt_t_employee.salary_currency'

}

_Agency,

Agency transactional view and composition:

@AccessControl.authorizationCheck: #NOT_REQUIRED 
@EndUserText.label: 'Agency'
@Metadata.ignorePropagatedAnnotations: true 

define root view entity ZI_BRT_AGENCYTP as select from ZI_BRT_AGENCY
composition of exact one to many ZI_BRT_EMPLOYEETP as _Employee  

{

Employee transactional view:

@AccessControl.authorizationCheck: #NOT_REQUIRED

@Metadata.ignorePropagatedAnnotations: true 

define view entity ZI_BRT_EMPLOYEETP as select from ZI_BRT_EMPLOYEE 

association to parent ZI_BRT_AGENCYTP as _Agency on $projection.Agency = _Agency.Agency 

association of many to one ZI_BRT_EMPLOYEETP as _Manager on $projection.Agency = _Manager.Agency 

and $projection.Manager = _Manager.Employee 

association of one to many ZI_BRT_EMPLOYEETP as _Employee on $projection.Agency = _Employee.Agency 

and $projection.Employee = _Employee.Manager 

association of one to one I_Currency as _Currency on $projection.SalaryCurrency = _Currency.Currency 

{ 
key Agency,
key Employee,
FirstName,
LastName,
@Semantics.amount.currencyCode: 'SalaryCurrency'
Salary,
SalaryCurrency,
Manager,
SiblingOrderNumber, 

LocalCreatedBy,
LocalCreatedAt,
LocalLastChangedBy,
LocalLastChangedAt,
/* Associations */
_Agency,
_Currency,
_Employee,
_Manager 

}

CDS hierarchy definition:

@AccessControl.authorizationCheck: #NOT_REQUIRED 
define hierarchy zi_brt_employeehn_hd 
with parameters P_Agency : /dmo/agency_id 

as parent child hierarchy( 

source ZI_BRT_EMPLOYEE

child to parent association _Manager
directory _Agency filter by

Agency = $parameters.P_Agency
start where

Manager is initial
siblings order by
SiblingOrderNumber ascending 

) 
{ 
key Agency,
key Employee,
Manager,
SiblingOrderNumber 

}

This turns the Employee self-association into a tree. 

  • P_Agency limits the hierarchy to one Agency. 
  • source says where the employee records come from. 
  • child to parent association _Manager defines the direction from each employee to their manager. 
  • The directory filter restricts the tree to the selected Agency. 
  • start where Manager is initial makes employees without managers the top-level nodes. 
  • siblings order by sorts employees under the same manager. 

Example: 

Agency A 
       |
      +-- Manager 100
         |
        +-- Employee 101 
        +-- Employee 102 
              |
             +-- Employee 103 

Agency consumption view:

@AccessControl.authorizationCheck: #NOT_REQUIRED

@Metadata.allowExtensions: true

define root view entity zc_brt_agencytp 
provider contract transactional_query 
as projection on ZI_BRT_AGENCYTP
{

Name,

_Country,

}

Employee consumption view: 

@AccessControl.authorizationCheck: #NOT_REQUIRED

@Metadata.allowExtensions: true 

@OData.hierarchy.recursiveHierarchy: [{ entity.name: 'ZI_BRT_EMPLOYEEHN_HD' }]
@Search.searchable: true 

define view entity zc_brt_employeetp 
as projection on ZI_BRT_EMPLOYEETP
{ 
@ObjectModel.text.element: ['AgencyName']
key Agency,
key Employee,
_Agency.Name as AgencyName,

@Search.defaultSearchElement: true
@Search.fuzzinessThreshold: 0.87
FirstName,
@Search.defaultSearchElement: true
@Search.fuzzinessThreshold: 0.87
LastName,
Salary, 

@Consumption.valueHelpDefinition: [
{ entity: { 
name: 'I_CurrencyStdVH',
element: 'Currency'
},
useForValidation: true 
} 

] 
SalaryCurrency, 

@Consumption.valueHelpDefinition: [
{ 
entity: { name: 'ZI_BRT_EMP_MANAGERVH', element: 'Employee' }, 

additionalBinding: [{ element: 'Agency', localElement: 'Agency', usage: #FILTER }]
} 
] 

Manager, 
_Manager.FirstName as ManagerFirstName,
_Manager.LastName as ManagerLastName,

SiblingOrderNumber, 
LocalLastChangedAt, 

/* Associations */ 
_Agency : redirected to parent zc_brt_agencytp,
_Manager : redirected to zc_brt_employeetp,
_Employee : redirected to zc_brt_employeetp,
_Currency
}

This exposes the CDS hierarchy information for OData consumption. 

@odata.hierarchy.recursiveHierarchy:[{ entity.name: 'ZI_BRT_EMPLOYEEHN_HD' }]

Therefore, the framework knows that Employee has a recursive hierarchy based on: ZI_BRT_EMPLOYEEHN_HD 
 
The employee consumption view also redirects associations: 

_Manager : redirected to zc_brt_employeetp, 
_Employee : redirected to zc_brt_employeetp

So the recursive employee relationships remain available at the consumption layer. 

Behavior definition:

managed;
strict ( 2 ); 
with draft; 

define behavior for ZI_BRT_AGENCYTP alias Agency 
implementation in class zbp_i_brt_agencytp unique
early numbering
persistent table zbrt_t_agency
draft table zbrt_t_agn_d_hd
lock master
total etag LastChangedAt
authorization master ( none )
etag master LocalLastChangedAt
{ 
create;
update;
delete; 

field ( readonly ) Agency, LocalCreatedBy, LocalCreatedAt, LocalLastChangedBy, LocalLastChangedAt, LastChangedAt; 

field ( mandatory ) CountryCode, EMailAddress, Name;

association _Employee { create; with draft; }

draft action Resume;
draft action Edit;
draft action Activate optimized;
draft action Discard;

validation validateEMailAddress on save { create; field EMailAddress; }
validation validateCountryCode on save { create; field CountryCode; }
validation validateName on save { create; field Name; } 

draft determine action Prepare 
{ 
validation validateEMailAddress;
validation validateCountryCode;
validation validateName;
validation Employee~validationSalaryPositive;
validation Employee~validationCurrencyExists;
validation Employee~validationNameGiven; 
} 
mapping for zbrt_t_agency 
{ 
Agency             = agency;
Name               = name;
Street             = street;
PostalCode         = postal_code;
City               = city;
CountryCode        = country_code;
PhoneNumber        = phone_number;
EMailAddress       = email_address;
WebAddress         = web_address;
LocalCreatedBy     = local_created_by;
LocalCreatedAt     = local_created_at;
LocalLastChangedBy = local_last_changed_by;
LocalLastChangedAt = local_last_changed_at;
LastChangedAt      = last_changed_at;
} 

} 

define behavior for ZI_BRT_EMPLOYEETP alias Employee
implementation in class zbp_i_brt_employeetp_hd unique
early numbering
persistent table zbrt_t_employee
draft table zbrt_t_emp_d_hd
lock dependent by _Agency
authorization dependent by _Agency
etag master LocalLastChangedAt 
{ 
update;
delete;

field ( readonly ) Agency, Employee, SiblingOrderNumber; 
field ( readonly ) Manager; 

association _Agency { with draft; } 
association _Manager 

{ 
with draft;
link action linkManager;
unlink action unlinkManager; 
} 
association _Employee { with draft; } 

instance hierarchy zi_brt_employeehn_hd
{ 
managed reorder action changeNextSibling; 
field ( hierarchy-index ) SiblingOrderNumber; 
ascending association _Manager; 
descending association _Employee { with cascading delete; }
} 
validation validationSalaryPositive on save { create; field Salary; }
validation validationCurrencyExists on save { create; field SalaryCurrency; } 

validation validationNameGiven on save { create; field FirstName, LastName; } 

determine action validateSalaryPositive { validation validationSalaryPositive; } 

determine action validateCurrencyExists { validation validationCurrencyExists; } 

determine action validateNameGiven { validation validationNameGiven; } 

side effects

{ 

determine action validateSalaryPositive executed on field Salary affects messages;

determine action validateCurrencyExists executed on field SalaryCurrency affects messages; 

determine action validateNameGiven executed on field FirstName, field LastName affects messages;
} 
mapping for zbrt_t_employee
{ 
Agency             = agency;
Employee           = employee;
FirstName          = first_name;
LastName           = last_name;
Salary             = salary;
SalaryCurrency     = salary_currency;
Manager            = manager;
SiblingOrderNumber = sibling_order_number;
LocalCreatedBy     = local_created_by;
LocalCreatedAt     = local_created_at;
LocalLastChangedBy = local_last_changed_by;
LocalLastChangedAt = local_last_changed_at; 

} 
}

This is useful because the Prepare action checks the business object's consistency before activation. 

Notice that Employee validations are also included: 

Employee~validationSalaryPositive 
Employee~validationCurrencyExists 
Employee~validationNameGiven 

So, the Agency draft can validate the complete composition.

Manager Link and Unlink:

The behavior contains: 

association _Manager
  {
        with draft;
        link action  linkManager;
        unlink action unlinkManager;
  }

This provides explicit actions for managing the manager relationship. 

Conceptually: 

Employee 101 
     | 
     |     linkManager 
    v 
Employee 100 

and: 

Employee 101 
     | 
     |    unlinkManager 
    v 
No Manager 

instance hierarchy zi_brt_employeehn_hd
    {
      managed reorder action changeNextSibling;
      field ( hierarchy-index ) SiblingOrderNumber;
      ascending association _Manager;
      descending association _Employee { with cascading delete; }
    }

managed reorder action changeNextSibling; -> allows the framework to manage sibling reordering. 

For example: 

Before: 

Manager 100 
├── Employee 101 
├── Employee 102 
└── Employee 103 

After moving Employee 103: 

Manager 100 
├── Employee 101 
├── Employee 103 
└── Employee 102 

The sibling order is maintained through: 

SiblingOrderNumber

field ( hierarchy-index )  SiblingOrderNumber; -> This identifies the field used for ordering siblings. 

Therefore: SiblingOrderNumber is not just an ordinary numeric field; RAP uses it as the hierarchy ordering index. 

ascending association _Manager; -> The hierarchy can be traversed upward: 

Employee 
  ↑ 
Manager 
  ↑ 
Manager's Manager 
descending association _Employee { with cascading delete; }​

This allows traversal downward: 

Manager 
  | 
  +-- Employee 
      | 
      +-- Employee 

The cascading delete configuration means deletion can propagate through the hierarchy according to the defined relationship.

entry.title: ABAP Sessions at SAP TechEd 2026
entry.content:
Hey Everyone!

SAP TechEd in 2026 is just around the corner, and preparations are in full swing at SAP! This year event series kicks of on October 27 with SAP TechEd Berlin, coupled with SAP TechEd Virtual, followed by various tour stops  around the globe up to Q1 2027. Like last year, SAP TechEd Virtual will comprise a selection of livestreamed on-site Berlin sessions accompanied by a special online program – and is free of charge. 

SAP TechEd is the leading tech conference for all developers, IT professionals, business experts, tech visionaries, innovators, and leaders eager to gain in-depth knowledge of SAP’s solutions, platforms, and technologies, along with insights into their future direction. It also offer an opportunity to network and connect with peers and SAP experts. 

Whether you are attending in person in Berlin or joining virtually from anywhere in the world, there is a rich lineup of sessions waiting for you – from strategy talks and road maps to deep dives.  Hands-on workshops to get your hands dirty and the show floor experience, including "Ask the Expert" pods, Developer garage and AI Workspace, are waiting for the on-site participants.

Save the dates and register now!  

DateEventLocation
October 27-29, 2026SAP TechEd Berlin & SAP TechEd Virtual 
Berlin, Germany & Online (Global)
November 2-4, 2026: ASUG Tech Connect Fort Worth, Texas, USA
November 17-18: Mastering SAP Collaborate Sydney Sydney, Australia
February 25-26, 2027SAP TechEd Bangalore (India)Bangalore, India
Q1 2027 DSAG TechXchangeTBD, Germany

 at SAP TechEd in 2026

If you're an ABAP developer, architect, or simply curious about what's next in the ABAP space — this post is your one-stop overview of all ABAP-related sessions at this year's event. 

 This year's lineup of insightful ABAP sessions revolves around following overarching topics: agent-led development – transitioning from AI-assisted to fully agentic workflows powered by the ABAP MCP Server; ABAP Cloud innovations in SAP BAIP, ABAP environment and SAP Cloud ERP – the latest in RAP, CDS, and the ABAP language, including AI-infused application development; and agent-led custom code migration and modernization – accelerating the journey from SAP ECC to SAP SAP/4HANA Cloud and supporting the clean core strategy. 

Keynotes & ABAP-related sessions at SAP TechEd Berlin

 Keynotes

KEY100 | Built for the ones who build | 📺Livestream: KEY100v
Imagine if you could walk into work and just build. No data pipelines. No models to teach the business. No AI cost surprises. SAP brings together AI, tools, business data, governance, agents, and a new UX layer in one integrated AI platform so you can build freely and turn ambitious ideas into business outcomes. Find out what’s ready for you today.
Schedule: Tuesday, Oct 27 | 9:00 AM - 10:30 AM CET
Speakers:

  • Philipp Herzig - Chief AI Officer and Chief Technology Officer, SAP 
  • Manoj Swaminathan - Chief Product Officer SAP Autonomous Suite, and Member of the Extended Board of SAP SE, SAP
  • Jonathan von Rueden - Chief AI Officer, SAP

KEY101 | Agent v0.0.7 - A license to skill | 📺Livestream: KEY101v
Your mission: master the AI-driven development revolution. Join Agent Kasimir to see how the SAP Business AI Platform, the Joule Studio solution, and open ecosystem tools give developers a license to skill. From agentic orchestration to context-aware code, discover how modern spycraft meets enterprise tech to redefine how we build software. 
Schedule: Wednesday, Oct 28 | 9:00 AM - 10:00 AM CET
Speakers: Josh Bentley (SAP), Rich Heilman (SAP), DJ Adams (SAP), Rekha D R (SAP), Sheena M K (SAP), Shilpa Shankar (SAP), Antonio Maradiaga (SAP), Witalij Rudnicki (SAP), Nora von Thenen (SAP)

 Strategy Talks (25")

ST124 | Strategy for agent-led development in ABAP | 📺Livestream: ST124v
Development using ABAP development tools transitions from being AI-assisted to agent-led. This spans greenfield development as well as the migration and modernization of existing solutions. Get insights into our strategy for agent-led development in ABAP and the evolution of AI capabilities for ABAP enabled by the SAP Joule for Developers add-on.
Speakers: Sonja Liénard (SAP), Dr. Alexander Rother (SAP)
Schedule: Tuesday, Oct 27 | 2:00 PM - 2:25 PM CET 

ST122 | Extending the SAP Autonomous Suite
See and experience the journey of extensibility across SAP Autonomous Suite. Discover how AI-driven development with SAP Build solutions including the ABAP Cloud model is transforming the way extensions are designed, generated, and deployed. Learn the way forward to make your extensions ready for the era of agentic AI.
Speakers: Khaled Musilhy (SAP), Dr. Alexander Rother (SAP)
Schedule: Tuesday, Oct 27 | 2:45 PM - 3:10 PM CET

️ Road Maps (25")

AD819 | Road map for agent-led ABAP development 
Development in ABAP is transitioning from being AI-assisted to agent-led. This spans greenfield development as well as the migration and modernization of existing solutions. Learn what is available and what's coming next.
Speakers: Dr. Alexander Rother (SAP), Simona Marincei (SAP)
Schedule 1: Tuesday, Oct 27 | 12:00 PM - 12:45 PM CET
Schedule 2: Wednesday, Oct 28 | 12:45 PM - 1:10 PM CET

TM817 | What's next in extensibility for SAP Autonomous Suite? 
Explore agent-driven extensibility innovations shaping the future of SAP Autonomous Suite. See what's ahead of us regarding enabling your extensions for the era of agentic AI and how to leverage our assistants for that reality.  
Speakers: Oren Shatil (SAP), Dr. Alexander Rother (SAP)
Schedule:  Wednesday, Oct 28 | 12:00 PM - 12:25 PM CET

 Deep Dives (45")

Explore how agentic development with ABAP development tools is transforming the developer experience. This session provides insights into the ABAP tool strategy, and the technical foundations behind it, with a focus on the ABAP Language Server and ABAP MCP Server, and gives an outlook on modern ABAP development.
Speakers: Anne Keller (SAP), Dileep Kumar Reddy Ajjungunti (SAP)
On-site schedule 1: Tuesday, Oct 27 | 12:00 PM - 12:45 PM CET

Ready to elevate your cloud-native development? Explore the latest innovations in ABAP Cloud, including powerful enhancements in the ABAP language, Core Data Services, embedded analytics, and the ABAP RESTful Application Programming Model, such as the transactional outbox patterns with the background processing framework and collaborative draft.
Speakers: Carine Tchoutouo Djomo (SAP), Volker Drees (SAP)

Build applications based on the ABAP Cloud model that are fully aligned with a clean core strategy (level A). Speakers: Frank Jentsch (SAP), Steffen Siegmund (SAP)
Schedule: Wednesday, Oct 28 | 12:30 PM - 1:15 PM CET
Related HOW: AD261

Explore how a new generation of agent-led AI assistants is rewriting the economics of migration and modernization by cutting costs, fast tracking project timelines, and spanning the full migration lifecycle. At the same time, learn how SAP is accelerating the path to the Autonomous Enterprise and empowering you to take advantage of these AI agents.
Speakers:  Sören Ruder (SAP), Sonja Liénard (SAP)
On-site schedule: Wednesday, Oct 28 | 11:30 PM - 12:15 PM CET
Virtual schedule: Thursday, Oct 29 | 11:00 AM - 11:45 AM CET

TM105 | Agent-Led custom code migration: From planning to mass Adaptation 
Custom code migration often bottlenecks the move from SAP ERP Central Component to SAP Cloud ERP Private. See how an agent-led toolchain accelerates the process from planning in SAP Cloud ALM to AI-powered mass remediation with the Custom Code Migration Agent in SAP Joule for Developers. Plus, discover the latest custom code management innovations.
Speakers: Olga Dolinskaja (SAP), Marco Matha (SAP)
Schedule 1: Tuesday, Oct 27 | 2:00 PM - 2:45 PM CET
Schedule 2: Thursday, Oct 29 | 2:00 PM - 2:45 PM CET
Related HOW: TM260

Explore how to extend SAP Cloud ERP and transform standard business services into intelligent cloud apps with the ABAP Cloud development model. Learn to embed advanced generative AI capabilities into apps built using the ABAP RESTful application programming model—all while keeping the core clean and future-ready.
Speakers: Volker Drees (SAP), Carine Tchoutouo Djomo (SAP)
Schedule 1: Wednesday, Oct 28 | 1:30 PM - 2:15 PM CET
Schedule 2: Thursday, Oct 29 | 1:00 PM - 1:45 PM CET
Related HOW: TM364

TM108 | The journey with clean core continues for SAP Cloud ERP Private | 📺Livestream: TM108v
Discover how the clean core strategy has evolved in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition. Explore the latest in extensibility, new capabilities in the dashboard for RISE with SAP Methodology, and how AI helps make custom code compliant with clean core. Learn about new guidance for data, integration, and clean core in relation to SAP's API policy.

Virtual Schedule: Thursday, Oct 29 | 12:00 PM - 12:45 PM CET

Learn to leverage agentic AI to rapidly build transactional SAP Fiori apps and services with ABAP Cloud using the ABAP RESTful application programming model (RAP) in the ABAP development tools for VS Code.  
Speakers: Wolfgang Woehrle (SAP), Anne Keller (SAP), Dr. Alexander Rother (SAP), Dileep Kumar Reddy Ajjugunti (SAP)
Schedule: Tuesday, Oct 27 | 4:00 PM - 6:00 PM CET
Related DD: AD100

AD260 | Level up app development with ABAP Cloud innovations and Joule solution
Explore innovations in the ABAP RESTful application programming model to build modern apps. Generate multi-node business objects and use capabilities like event-driven side effects, collaborative draft, background processing, and analytical tables for a greater end user experience. Use the SAP Joule for Developers add-on to accelerate development.
Speakers: Carine Tchoutouo Djomo (SAP), Marina Blank (SAP), Anne Keller (SAP), Frank Jentsch (SAP)
Schedule: Thursday, Oct 29 | 09:00 AM - 11:00 AM CET
Related DD: AD200

Learn how to monitor and troubleshoot side-by-side applications built with the ABAP Cloud model on SAP BAIP, ABAP environment, aligning with a clean core strategy (level A). Use technical monitoring tools for an application based on ABAP Cloud and gain practical troubleshooting experience with ABAP development tools for Eclipse.

Schedule: Thursday, Oct 29 | 11:30 AM - 1:30 PM CET

Experience the RISE with SAP journey moving custom extensions from SAP ERP Central Component to SAP Cloud ERP Private.
